subject: Can we have INLA switch to a local search?

messages.author: 09fd833635384d0f
messages.subject: Can we have INLA switch to a local search?
parts:
For many model runs, we are seeing the following output: "Mode not sufficient accurate; switch to a stupid local search strategy."

We were wondering if there may be a way to automatically have INLA switch to the "stupid local search strategy"?

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Can we have INLA switch to a local search?
parts:
hi

sorry for joining late.

this option, 'stupid search', was added to rescue difficult cases.
the alg goes like this:

- run the optimizer to get the estimated mode
- estimate the hessian at this mode
- if the '-hessian' is pos def, return. if its NOT pos def, we have not
a mode, THEN switch to the stupid search mode:

S:
- look at all the func-evals used to estimate the hessian.
- move to the mode within those
- re-estimate the hessian at this new point.
- if `-hessian', positive definite, return, else, go back to S.

as you see, this should not happen, and if it does, it will go into a
sloooow loop, but it will not stop because of 'mode not found'.

so the issue is really to prevent the alg going into 'stupid search
mode'. when it goes into that mode, it usually means that the log-
posterior is very flat. more informative priors will do wonders, but it
can also be that a to flexible model is used.

hope this helps
H
